hook.line: When you have said a lot and want one thing to stick, Spanish lets you put a spotlight on it. Tomás uses it to tell Mariana the one thing he is sure of.
hook.es: Si algo tengo claro es que no vuelvo.
hook.en: If there's one thing I'm sure of, it's that I'm not going back.

examples.es: Si algo tengo claro es que no vuelvo.
examples.en: If there's one thing I'm sure of, it's that I'm not going back.

examples.es: Si de algo estoy seguro es de la honestidad de Hernando.
examples.en: If there's one thing I'm certain of, it's Hernando's honesty.

examples.es: Si alguien sabe la respuesta, es Vale.
examples.en: If anyone knows the answer, it's Vale.

examples.es: Si algo me gusta de este barrio, es su gente.
examples.en: If there's one thing I like about this neighbourhood, it's its people.

examples.es: Si algo sabe hacer Vale, es un buen pan.
examples.en: If there's one thing Vale knows how to make, it's good bread.

examples.es: Si alguien merece este café, es Tomás.
examples.en: If anyone deserves this café, it's Tomás.

rule: Start with *si algo* or *si alguien*, say what it does or feels, then a comma and *es*, and then the one thing you are spotlighting. This *si* is not doubt; it means "if there's one thing". If the verb needs a preposition, repeat it before the spotlight: *Si de algo estoy seguro, es de…*. If the spotlight is a whole sentence, add *que*: *es que no vuelvo*. Otherwise, no extra word: *es su gente*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a conditional equational structure: it sets up the rest as known and spotlights one item.

readAndPick.es: Si algo tengo claro es que no vuelvo.
options: I'm not sure if I'm going back.
If there's one thing I'm sure of, it's that I'm not going back.
If I'm sure, I'll go back.

readAndPick.es: Si alguien sabe la respuesta, es Vale.
options: If anyone knows the answer, it's Vale.
Vale will know the answer.
Nobody knows the answer but me.

readAndPick.es: Si de algo estoy seguro es de la honestidad de Hernando.
options: I doubt Hernando is honest.
Hernando is sure of my honesty.
If there's one thing I'm certain of, it's Hernando's honesty.

readAndPick.es: Si algo me gusta de este barrio, es su gente.
options: If there's one thing I like about this neighbourhood, it's its people.
I don't like the people of this neighbourhood.
If I like the neighbourhood, it's because of the people.

readAndPick.es: Si alguien merece este café, es Tomás.
options: Tomás doesn't deserve this café.
If anyone deserves this café, it's Tomás.
If Tomás deserves it, he will get it.

readAndPick.es: Si algo sabe hacer Vale, es un buen pan.
options: If Vale knew how, she would make bread.
Vale doesn't know how to make bread.
If there's one thing Vale knows how to make, it's good bread.

readAndPick.es: Si algo tengo claro es que Altamira no gana.
options: If there's one thing I'm sure of, it's that Altamira won't win.
I'm not sure if Altamira wins.
Altamira is sure it will win.

readAndPick.es: Si algo me preocupa es el dinero.
options: I'm not worried about money.
If there's one thing that worries me, it's money.
Money worries me less than before.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *es* or *que* and type the whole sentence: *Si algo tengo claro ___ que no vuelvo.*
yourTurn.answer: Si algo tengo claro es que no vuelvo.
yourTurn.why: The spotlight word is *es*, and *que* then brings the whole sentence.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If anyone knows the answer, it's Vale.
yourTurn.answer: Si alguien sabe la respuesta, es Vale.
accept: Si alguien sabe la respuesta es Vale.
yourTurn.why: *Si alguien* plus the verb, then *es* and the name.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If there's one thing I like about this neighbourhood, it's its people.
yourTurn.answer: Si algo me gusta de este barrio, es su gente.
accept: Si algo me gusta de este barrio es su gente.
yourTurn.why: The *de* belongs to *me gusta de este barrio*; it isn't repeated before the spotlight.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If there's one thing I'm certain of, it's Hernando's honesty.
yourTurn.answer: Si de algo estoy seguro es de la honestidad de Hernando.
accept: Si de algo estoy seguro, es de la honestidad de Hernando.
yourTurn.why: *Estar seguro* takes *de*, so *de* comes back after *es*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If anyone deserves this café, it's Tomás.
yourTurn.answer: Si alguien merece este café, es Tomás.
accept: Si alguien merece este café es Tomás.
yourTurn.why: Same frame with *alguien*, then the name.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If there's one thing Vale knows how to make, it's good bread.
yourTurn.answer: Si algo sabe hacer Vale, es un buen pan.
accept: Si algo sabe hacer Vale es un buen pan.
yourTurn.why: The spotlight is a noun, so there is no *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If there's one thing that worries me, it's money.
yourTurn.answer: Si algo me preocupa es el dinero.
accept: Si algo me preocupa, es el dinero.

pitfalls.wrong: Si algo tengo claro es no vuelvo.
pitfalls.right: Si algo tengo claro es que no vuelvo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A whole sentence after *es* needs *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Si de algo estoy seguro es la honestidad de Hernando.
pitfalls.right: Si de algo estoy seguro es de la honestidad de Hernando.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The preposition comes back: *de algo… es de…*.

pitfalls.wrong: Si algo me gusta de este barrio, es de su gente.
pitfalls.right: Si algo me gusta de este barrio, es su gente.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Gustar* doesn't need *de* in front of the spotlight, so don't add one.

personal: Say the one thing you are surest of about yourself, with *Si algo tengo claro es que*.
